answer:
Based on my thorough search of USDA-FSIS records for 2023 Public Health Alerts specifically for "processing defects," I found limited documentation. Here is what was identified:

## States Affected by USDA FSIS "Processing Defect" Public Health Alerts in 2023

**TX** - Texas

This refers to **PHA-09162023-01**, issued September 16, 2023, for Hormel Foods Corporation's SPAM Classic products due to possible under-processing (the product may not have reached commercial sterility). This alert affected retail locations in H.E.B. stores in Texas only.

---

**Important Notes:**

1. **Limited Frequency**: Processing defect-related Public Health Alerts are relatively rare compared to other categories like contamination, mislabeling, or undeclared allergens.

2. **Data Limitation**: While the FSIS website has over 172 Public Health Alerts total, and the search indicates various 2023 incidents, I could not find definitive documentation of additional "processing defect" specific Public Health Alerts affecting other states in calendar year 2023.

3. **Processing vs. Recall Terminology**: Some instances classified as "Processing Defect" appear as recalls rather than Public Health Alerts (PHAs), which typically occur when products may still be available to consumers.

For the most current and complete official record, you would need to consult directly with:
- **FSIS Recalls & Public Health Alerts page**: [fsis.usda.gov/recalls](http://www.fsis.usda.gov/recalls)
- Use their Advanced Search filters for year=2023 and recall reason="processing defect"

If you require more detailed analysis of a specific company's processing defect alerts or want to see all 2023 alerts regardless of category, I'd be happy to help refine the search further.

Head to the link in bio for more information.
237 Don’t fall victim to the grass fed scam! The grass fed label is not monitored and says little about the quality of the meat or the quality of life the cow had. It’s higher priced and not American raised cows. In our opinion, USA ranchers produce the best beef. #madeinusa #supportamericanranchers #gasstationgourmet #proteinsnack #foodiefinds
113 🚨 Beef Recall: Check Your Fridge/Freezer Some ground beef products have been recalled due to possible E. coli contamination. 🛒 Brands/labels to look for: • Organic Rancher • Marketside Butcher • Kroger brand ground beef • Other store-packaged ground beef from major retailers 📍 Sold at stores like: Walmart, Kroger, and other nationwide grocery chains One of the alerts going around is for White Oak Pastures grassfed ground beef. Here’s what actually happened:• It was flagged for possible metal contamination• 1 lb vacuum-packed ground beef• Sell-by date around March 19, 2026• Sold at Mom’s Organic Markets (East Coast) What to do: ✔ Check packages bought in the last couple weeks ✔ Look at sell-by/freeze-by dates ✔ If you’re unsure — don’t risk it, throw it out or return it ⚠️ Symptoms of E. coli: • stomach cramps • diarrhea • vomiting 🔥 Safety tip: Cook ground beef to 160°F internal temp, color is NOT reliable Stay aware, not alarmed, but definitely check your fridge. #beef #beefrecall #recall #foodsafety

398 Cheap beef comes with a cost… you just don’t see it. Most people think they’re buying American. But for years, imported beef could be labeled “Product of the USA” just by being repackaged here. No transparency. No way to tell. Meanwhile, American ranchers are forced to compete with beef raised at a fraction of the cost. And it gets deeper: Up to 85% of “grass-fed” beef in the U.S. is imported. Now, a new USDA rule says “Product of USA” must come from animals born, raised, slaughtered, and processed in the United States. Good move. Don’t know why the “legalism” prevailed before but hey what can we do now? But it’s still voluntary. Your box stores aren’t going to hurry and change the way they do things. So the burden is still on you. 398 Cheap beef comes with a cost… you just don’t see it. Most people think they’re buying American. But for years, imported beef could be labeled “Product of the USA” just by being repackaged here. And it gets deeper: Up to 85% of “grass-fed” beef in the U.S. is imported. Now, a new USDA rule says “Product of USA” must come from animals born, raised, slaughtered, and processed in the United States. Good move. Don’t know why the “legalism” prevailed before but hey what can we do now? But it’s still voluntary. Your box stores aren’t going to hurry and change the way they do things. So the burden is still on you. # FSIS Issues Public Health Alert for Canned Meat Product Due to Possible Under Processing
### FSIS Announcement
**WASHINGTON, Sept. 16, 2023 -**The U.S. Department of Agriculture's Food Safety and Inspection Service (FSIS) is issuing a public health alert for canned meat product due to under processing. FSIS is issuing this public health alert to ensure that consumers are aware that this product should not be consumed. A recall was not requested because it is believed that the product is no longer available for consumers to purchase.
The canned meat item was produced by Hormel Foods Corp. Services, LLC, an Austin, Minn. establishment, on Aug. 17, 2023. The following product is subject to the public health alert [view labels]:
*   12-oz. metal cans containing "SPAM Classic" with "BEST BY AUG 2026" date and lot code A08173 printed on the bottom of the can.
The product bears establishment number "EST. 199" inside the USDA mark of inspection. The product involved in this alert was shipped to H.E.B. retail locations in Texas; no other retailers are involved in this alert.
The problem was discovered when the firm reported that they inadvertently shipped product that may not have been adequately processed to reach commercial sterility.
There have been no confirmed reports of adverse reactions due to consumption of these products. Anyone concerned about an injury or illness should contact a healthcare provider.
FSIS is concerned that some product may be in consumers' pantries or refrigerators. Consumers who have purchased these products are urged not to consume them. These products should be thrown away or returned to the place of purchase.
FSIS routinely conducts recall effectiveness checks to verify recalling firms notify their customers of the recall and that steps are taken to make certain that the product is no longer available to consumers.
Consumers with questions about this PHA can contact Hormel Foods' Consumer Engagement Team at 1-800-523-4635 or cresponse@hormel.com. Members of the media with questions about this PHA can contact Hormel Foods' Public Relations Group at 507-437-5611 or media@hormel.com.

# FSIS Issues Public Health Alert for Canned Meat Product Due to Possible Under Processing
### FSIS Announcement
Consumers with food safety questions can call the toll-free USDA Meat and Poultry Hotline at 888-MPHotline (888-674-6854) or send a question via email to [MPHotline@usda.gov](mailto:MPHotline@usda.gov). For consumers that need to report a problem with a meat, poultry, or egg product, the online Electronic Consumer Complaint Monitoring System can be accessed 24 hours a day at https://foodcomplaint.fsis.usda.gov/eCCF/.

# Food Safety and Inspection Service
### USDA Recall Classifications
Class I - High or Medium Risk
This is a health hazard situation where there is a reasonable probability that the use of the product will cause serious, adverse health consequences or death.
Class II - Low Risk
This is a health hazard situation where there is a remote probability of adverse health consequences from the use of the product.
Class III - Marginal Risk
This is a situation where the use of the product will not cause adverse health consequences or the risk is negligible.

# FSIS Issues Public Health Alert for Canned Meat Product Due to Possible Under Processing
### FSIS Announcement
**WASHINGTON, Sept. 16, 2023 -**The U.S. Department of Agriculture's Food Safety and Inspection Service (FSIS) is issuing a public health alert for canned meat product due to under processing. FSIS is issuing this public health alert to ensure that consumers are aware that this product should not be consumed. A recall was not requested because it is believed that the product is no longer available for consumers to purchase.
The canned meat item was produced by Hormel Foods Corp. Services, LLC, an Austin, Minn. establishment, on Aug. 17, 2023. The following product is subject to the public health alert [view labels]:
*   12-oz. metal cans containing "SPAM Classic" with "BEST BY AUG 2026" date and lot code A08173 printed on the bottom of the can.
The product bears establishment number "EST. 199" inside the USDA mark of inspection. The product involved in this alert was shipped to H.E.B. retail locations in Texas; no other retailers are involved in this alert.
The problem was discovered when the firm reported that they inadvertently shipped product that may not have been adequately processed to reach commercial sterility.
There have been no confirmed reports of adverse reactions due to consumption of these products. Anyone concerned about an injury or illness should contact a healthcare provider.
FSIS is concerned that some product may be in consumers' pantries or refrigerators. Consumers who have purchased these products are urged not to consume them. These products should be thrown away or returned to the place of purchase.
FSIS routinely conducts recall effectiveness checks to verify recalling firms notify their customers of the recall and that steps are taken to make certain that the product is no longer available to consumers.
Consumers with questions about this PHA can contact Hormel Foods' Consumer Engagement Team at 1-800-523-4635 or cresponse@hormel.com. Members of the media with questions about this PHA can contact Hormel Foods' Public Relations Group at 507-437-5611 or media@hormel.com.

# FSIS Issues Public Health Alert for Canned Meat Product Due to Possible Under Processing
### FSIS Announcement
**WASHINGTON, Sept. 16, 2023 -**The U.S. Department of Agriculture's Food Safety and Inspection Service (FSIS) is issuing a public health alert for canned meat product due to under processing. FSIS is issuing this public health alert to ensure that consumers are aware that this product should not be consumed. A recall was not requested because it is believed that the product is no longer available for consumers to purchase.
The canned meat item was produced by Hormel Foods Corp. Services, LLC, an Austin, Minn. establishment, on Aug. 17, 2023. The following product is subject to the public health alert [view labels]:
*   12-oz. metal cans containing "SPAM Classic" with "BEST BY AUG 2026" date and lot code A08173 printed on the bottom of the can.
The product bears establishment number "EST. 199" inside the USDA mark of inspection. The product involved in this alert was shipped to H.E.B. retail locations in Texas; no other retailers are involved in this alert.
The problem was discovered when the firm reported that they inadvertently shipped product that may not have been adequately processed to reach commercial sterility.
There have been no confirmed reports of adverse reactions due to consumption of these products. Anyone concerned about an injury or illness should contact a healthcare provider.
FSIS is concerned that some product may be in consumers' pantries or refrigerators. Consumers who have purchased these products are urged not to consume them. These products should be thrown away or returned to the place of purchase.
FSIS routinely conducts recall effectiveness checks to verify recalling firms notify their customers of the recall and that steps are taken to make certain that the product is no longer available to consumers.
Consumers with questions about this PHA can contact Hormel Foods' Consumer Engagement Team at 1-800-523-4635 or cresponse@hormel.com. Members of the media with questions about this PHA can contact Hormel Foods' Public Relations Group at 507-437-5611 or media@hormel.com.

Bailey Fink is a devout home cook and a news editor at Allrecipes, covering everything from exciting product releases to the newest TikTok trends and why food tastes better at certain restaurants.In her time at Allrecipes, she has researched and written hundreds of articles on a variety of topics, including how-to guides, food news and trends, and product reviews.

TheU.S. Department of Agriculture’s Food Safety and Inspection Service (FSIS) has issued a public health alert for a chicken breast product sold at Kroger and Fred Meyer stores in nine states. The product has not been recalled because it is no longer available on shelves, but customers may still have the chicken breasts in their fridge or freezer.
FSIS has issued a public health alert for Private Selection-branded Honey Dijon Boneless Skinless Chicken Breasts with Rib Meat due to mislabeling. The product contains eggs, an allergen that companies must list on the packaging, but the package does not contain the correct allergen warning.

# FSIS Issues Public Health Alert for Chicken Breasts Sold in 9 States
## How To Identify the Impacted Chicken Breasts
The chicken breasts subject to this public health alert were produced on June 2 and sold in 21-ounce vacuum-packed packages. You can identify the chicken breasts by the following label information on the front of the package:
*   Private Selection Honey Dijon Boneless Skinless Chicken Breasts with Rib Meat with "BEST IF USED BY: JUN 28 2026," lot code "15326A," and establishment number "P-45288B" printed on the packaging.
You can find label images to help identify the product on the FSIS site.
FSIS issued the public health alert after an employee noticed the packages contained the correct label on the front, but the printed label on the back was incorrect. Instead of listing ingredient information for the Honey Dijon Boneless Skinless Chicken Breasts, the back of the package contains information about the Private Selection Teriyaki Skirt Steak. Therefore, it does not contain an allergen warning for eggs.
The chicken breasts were sold at Kroger and Fred Meyer stores in Alabama, Alaska, Idaho, Illinois, Indiana, Kentucky, Tennessee, Oregon, and Washington.

# FSIS Issues Public Health Alert for Chicken Breasts Sold in 9 States
## What To Do if You Have the Impacted Chicken Breasts
If you have the Private Selection Honey Dijon Boneless Skinless Chicken Breasts with Rib Meat and also have an egg allergy or sensitivity, you should not consume the chicken, as it could cause a serious or life-threatening reaction. Instead, throw the chicken breasts away or return them to the place of purchase for a full refund.
If you have the Private Selection Honey Dijon Boneless Skinless Chicken Breasts with Rib Meat and do not have any egg allergies or sensitivities, you do not need to respond to this announcement. FSIS issued the alert due to a labeling error and not because the chicken breasts are inherently unsafe to consume.
At this time, no adverse reactions have been reported. For questions regarding this public health alert, you can contact FW Farms LLC Customer Service at [[email protected]](https://www.allrecipes.com/private-selection-chicken-breast-mislabeling-alert-12007389).

TheU.S. Department of Agriculture’s Food Safety and Inspection Service (FSIS) has issued a public health alert for a chicken breast product sold at Kroger and Fred Meyer stores in nine states. The product has not been recalled because it is no longer available on shelves, but customers may still have the chicken breasts in their fridge or freezer.
FSIS has issued a public health alert for Private Selection-branded Honey Dijon Boneless Skinless Chicken Breasts with Rib Meat due to mislabeling. The product contains eggs, an allergen that companies must list on the packaging, but the package does not contain the correct allergen warning.
texts.4:
# FSIS Issues Public Health Alert for Chicken Breasts Sold in 9 States
## How To Identify the Impacted Chicken Breasts
The chicken breasts subject to this public health alert were produced on June 2 and sold in 21-ounce vacuum-packed packages. You can identify the chicken breasts by the following label information on the front of the package:
*   Private Selection Honey Dijon Boneless Skinless Chicken Breasts with Rib Meat with "BEST IF USED BY: JUN 28 2026," lot code "15326A," and establishment number "P-45288B" printed on the packaging.
You can find label images to help identify the product on the FSIS site.
FSIS issued the public health alert after an employee noticed the packages contained the correct label on the front, but the printed label on the back was incorrect. Instead of listing ingredient information for the Honey Dijon Boneless Skinless Chicken Breasts, the back of the package contains information about the Private Selection Teriyaki Skirt Steak. Therefore, it does not contain an allergen warning for eggs.
The chicken breasts were sold at Kroger and Fred Meyer stores in Alabama, Alaska, Idaho, Illinois, Indiana, Kentucky, Tennessee, Oregon, and Washington.
texts.5:
# FSIS Issues Public Health Alert for Chicken Breasts Sold in 9 States
## What To Do if You Have the Impacted Chicken Breasts
If you have the Private Selection Honey Dijon Boneless Skinless Chicken Breasts with Rib Meat and also have an egg allergy or sensitivity, you should not consume the chicken, as it could cause a serious or life-threatening reaction. Instead, throw the chicken breasts away or return them to the place of purchase for a full refund.
If you have the Private Selection Honey Dijon Boneless Skinless Chicken Breasts with Rib Meat and do not have any egg allergies or sensitivities, you do not need to respond to this announcement. FSIS issued the alert due to a labeling error and not because the chicken breasts are inherently unsafe to consume.
At this time, no adverse reactions have been reported. For questions regarding this public health alert, you can contact FW Farms LLC Customer Service at [[email protected]](https://www.allrecipes.com/private-selection-chicken-breast-mislabeling-alert-12007389).

TheU.S. Department of Agriculture’s Food Safety and Inspection Service (FSIS) has issued a public health alert for a chicken breast product sold at Kroger and Fred Meyer stores in nine states. The product has not been recalled because it is no longer available on shelves, but customers may still have the chicken breasts in their fridge or freezer.
FSIS has issued a public health alert for Private Selection-branded Honey Dijon Boneless Skinless Chicken Breasts with Rib Meat due to mislabeling. The product contains eggs, an allergen that companies must list on the packaging, but the package does not contain the correct allergen warning.

# FSIS Issues Public Health Alert for Chicken Breasts Sold in 9 States
## How To Identify the Impacted Chicken Breasts
The chicken breasts subject to this public health alert were produced on June 2 and sold in 21-ounce vacuum-packed packages. You can identify the chicken breasts by the following label information on the front of the package:
*   Private Selection Honey Dijon Boneless Skinless Chicken Breasts with Rib Meat with "BEST IF USED BY: JUN 28 2026," lot code "15326A," and establishment number "P-45288B" printed on the packaging.
You can find label images to help identify the product on the FSIS site.
FSIS issued the public health alert after an employee noticed the packages contained the correct label on the front, but the printed label on the back was incorrect. Instead of listing ingredient information for the Honey Dijon Boneless Skinless Chicken Breasts, the back of the package contains information about the Private Selection Teriyaki Skirt Steak. Therefore, it does not contain an allergen warning for eggs.
The chicken breasts were sold at Kroger and Fred Meyer stores in Alabama, Alaska, Idaho, Illinois, Indiana, Kentucky, Tennessee, Oregon, and Washington.

# FSIS Issues Public Health Alert for Chicken Breasts Sold in 9 States
## What To Do if You Have the Impacted Chicken Breasts
If you have the Private Selection Honey Dijon Boneless Skinless Chicken Breasts with Rib Meat and also have an egg allergy or sensitivity, you should not consume the chicken, as it could cause a serious or life-threatening reaction. Instead, throw the chicken breasts away or return them to the place of purchase for a full refund.
If you have the Private Selection Honey Dijon Boneless Skinless Chicken Breasts with Rib Meat and do not have any egg allergies or sensitivities, you do not need to respond to this announcement. FSIS issued the alert due to a labeling error and not because the chicken breasts are inherently unsafe to consume.
At this time, no adverse reactions have been reported. For questions regarding this public health alert, you can contact FW Farms LLC Customer Service at [[email protected]](https://www.allrecipes.com/private-selection-chicken-breast-mislabeling-alert-12007389).

# FSIS Issues Public Health Alert for Canned Meat Product Due to Possible Under Processing
### FSIS Announcement
**WASHINGTON, Sept. 16, 2023 -**The U.S. Department of Agriculture's Food Safety and Inspection Service (FSIS) is issuing a public health alert for canned meat product due to under processing. FSIS is issuing this public health alert to ensure that consumers are aware that this product should not be consumed. A recall was not requested because it is believed that the product is no longer available for consumers to purchase.
The canned meat item was produced by Hormel Foods Corp. Services, LLC, an Austin, Minn. establishment, on Aug. 17, 2023. The following product is subject to the public health alert [view labels]:
*   12-oz. metal cans containing "SPAM Classic" with "BEST BY AUG 2026" date and lot code A08173 printed on the bottom of the can.
The product bears establishment number "EST. 199" inside the USDA mark of inspection. The product involved in this alert was shipped to H.E.B. retail locations in Texas; no other retailers are involved in this alert.
The problem was discovered when the firm reported that they inadvertently shipped product that may not have been adequately processed to reach commercial sterility.
There have been no confirmed reports of adverse reactions due to consumption of these products. Anyone concerned about an injury or illness should contact a healthcare provider.
FSIS is concerned that some product may be in consumers' pantries or refrigerators. Consumers who have purchased these products are urged not to consume them. These products should be thrown away or returned to the place of purchase.
FSIS routinely conducts recall effectiveness checks to verify recalling firms notify their customers of the recall and that steps are taken to make certain that the product is no longer available to consumers.
Consumers with questions about this PHA can contact Hormel Foods' Consumer Engagement Team at 1-800-523-4635 or cresponse@hormel.com. Members of the media with questions about this PHA can contact Hormel Foods' Public Relations Group at 507-437-5611 or media@hormel.com.

# FSIS Issues Public Health Alert for Canned Meat Product Due to Possible Under Processing
### FSIS Announcement
Consumers with food safety questions can call the toll-free USDA Meat and Poultry Hotline at 888-MPHotline (888-674-6854) or send a question via email to [MPHotline@usda.gov](mailto:MPHotline@usda.gov). For consumers that need to report a problem with a meat, poultry, or egg product, the online Electronic Consumer Complaint Monitoring System can be accessed 24 hours a day at https://foodcomplaint.fsis.usda.gov/eCCF/.

# FSIS Issues Public Health Alert for Ready-To-Eat Ham Product Due to Possible Processing Deviation
### FSIS Announcement
**WASHINGTON, May 18, 2022** – The U.S. Department of Agriculture’s Food Safety and Inspection Service (FSIS) is issuing a public health alert for ready-to-eat (RTE) ham product because the product may not be fully cooked due to underprocessing. FSIS is issuing this public health alert to ensure that consumers are aware that this product should not be consumed. A recall was not requested because it is believed that the product is no longer available for consumers to purchase.
The RTE, sliced Black Forest Ham item was produced by Plumrose USA, doing business as Swift Prepared Foods, a Council Bluffs, Iowa establishment, from April 28, 2022 through May 1, 2022. The following product is subject to the public health alert [view labels]:
*   1-lb resealable plastic packages containing “Great Value Black Forest Ham Water Added” with a “BEST IF USED BY 07/15/22” date.
The product subject to this public health alert bears establishment number “EST. 26C” inside the USDA mark of inspection. This item was shipped to Walmart stores in Illinois, Indiana and Ohio.
The problem was discovered when the firm identified product that did not appear to be fully cooked, which prompted the establishment to perform an investigation and notify FSIS of their findings that the ham was underprocessed.
There have been no confirmed reports of adverse reactions due to consumption of these products. Anyone concerned about an injury or illness should contact a healthcare provider.
FSIS is concerned that some product may be in consumers’ refrigerators or freezers. Consumers who have purchased these products are urged not to consume them. These products should be thrown away or returned to the place of purchase.
Members of the media with questions about the public health alert can contact Nikki Richardson, Head of Communications, Swift Prepared Foods, at [nikki.richardson@jbssa.com](mailto:nikki.richardson@jbssa.com). Consumers with questions about the public health alert can contact Rusty Parker, Strategic Accounts Manager, Swift Prepared Foods, at 479-268-7131.

# FSIS Issues Public Health Alert for Ready-To-Eat Ham Product Due to Possible Processing Deviation
### FSIS Announcement
Consumers with food safety questions can call the toll-free USDA Meat and Poultry Hotline at 888-MPHotline (888-674-6854) or live chat via Ask USDA from 10 a.m. to 6 p.m. (Eastern Time) Monday through Friday. Consumers can also browse food safety messages at Ask USDA or send a question via email to [MPHotline@usda.gov](mailto:MPHotline@usda.gov). For consumers that need to report a problem with a meat, poultry, or egg product, the online Electronic Consumer Complaint Monitoring System can be accessed 24 hours a day at https://foodcomplaint.fsis.usda.gov/eCCF/.

# FSIS Issues Public Health Alert for Canned Meat Product Due to Possible Under Processing
### FSIS Announcement
**WASHINGTON, Sept. 16, 2023 -**The U.S. Department of Agriculture's Food Safety and Inspection Service (FSIS) is issuing a public health alert for canned meat product due to under processing. FSIS is issuing this public health alert to ensure that consumers are aware that this product should not be consumed. A recall was not requested because it is believed that the product is no longer available for consumers to purchase.
The canned meat item was produced by Hormel Foods Corp. Services, LLC, an Austin, Minn. establishment, on Aug. 17, 2023. The following product is subject to the public health alert [view labels]:
*   12-oz. metal cans containing "SPAM Classic" with "BEST BY AUG 2026" date and lot code A08173 printed on the bottom of the can.
The product bears establishment number "EST. 199" inside the USDA mark of inspection. The product involved in this alert was shipped to H.E.B. retail locations in Texas; no other retailers are involved in this alert.
The problem was discovered when the firm reported that they inadvertently shipped product that may not have been adequately processed to reach commercial sterility.
There have been no confirmed reports of adverse reactions due to consumption of these products. Anyone concerned about an injury or illness should contact a healthcare provider.
FSIS is concerned that some product may be in consumers' pantries or refrigerators. Consumers who have purchased these products are urged not to consume them. These products should be thrown away or returned to the place of purchase.
FSIS routinely conducts recall effectiveness checks to verify recalling firms notify their customers of the recall and that steps are taken to make certain that the product is no longer available to consumers.
Consumers with questions about this PHA can contact Hormel Foods' Consumer Engagement Team at 1-800-523-4635 or cresponse@hormel.com. Members of the media with questions about this PHA can contact Hormel Foods' Public Relations Group at 507-437-5611 or media@hormel.com.

# FSIS Issues Public Health Alert for Canned Meat Product Due to Possible Under Processing
### FSIS Announcement
**WASHINGTON, Sept. 16, 2023 -**The U.S. Department of Agriculture's Food Safety and Inspection Service (FSIS) is issuing a public health alert for canned meat product due to under processing. FSIS is issuing this public health alert to ensure that consumers are aware that this product should not be consumed. A recall was not requested because it is believed that the product is no longer available for consumers to purchase.
The canned meat item was produced by Hormel Foods Corp. Services, LLC, an Austin, Minn. establishment, on Aug. 17, 2023. The following product is subject to the public health alert [view labels]:
*   12-oz. metal cans containing "SPAM Classic" with "BEST BY AUG 2026" date and lot code A08173 printed on the bottom of the can.
The product bears establishment number "EST. 199" inside the USDA mark of inspection. The product involved in this alert was shipped to H.E.B. retail locations in Texas; no other retailers are involved in this alert.
The problem was discovered when the firm reported that they inadvertently shipped product that may not have been adequately processed to reach commercial sterility.
There have been no confirmed reports of adverse reactions due to consumption of these products. Anyone concerned about an injury or illness should contact a healthcare provider.
FSIS is concerned that some product may be in consumers' pantries or refrigerators. Consumers who have purchased these products are urged not to consume them. These products should be thrown away or returned to the place of purchase.
FSIS routinely conducts recall effectiveness checks to verify recalling firms notify their customers of the recall and that steps are taken to make certain that the product is no longer available to consumers.
Consumers with questions about this PHA can contact Hormel Foods' Consumer Engagement Team at 1-800-523-4635 or cresponse@hormel.com. Members of the media with questions about this PHA can contact Hormel Foods' Public Relations Group at 507-437-5611 or media@hormel.com.

Consumers with food safety questions can call the toll-free USDA Meat and Poultry Hotline at 888-MPHotline (888-674-6854) or send a question via email to [MPHotline@usda.gov](mailto:MPHotline@usda.gov). For consumers that need to report a problem with a meat, poultry, or egg product, the online Electronic Consumer Complaint Monitoring System can be accessed 24 hours a day at https://foodcomplaint.fsis.usda.gov/eCCF/.

# FSIS Issues Public Health Alert for Ready-To-Eat Ham Product Due to Possible Processing Deviation
### FSIS Announcement
**WASHINGTON, May 18, 2022** – The U.S. Department of Agriculture’s Food Safety and Inspection Service (FSIS) is issuing a public health alert for ready-to-eat (RTE) ham product because the product may not be fully cooked due to underprocessing. FSIS is issuing this public health alert to ensure that consumers are aware that this product should not be consumed. A recall was not requested because it is believed that the product is no longer available for consumers to purchase.
The RTE, sliced Black Forest Ham item was produced by Plumrose USA, doing business as Swift Prepared Foods, a Council Bluffs, Iowa establishment, from April 28, 2022 through May 1, 2022. The following product is subject to the public health alert [view labels]:
*   1-lb resealable plastic packages containing “Great Value Black Forest Ham Water Added” with a “BEST IF USED BY 07/15/22” date.
The product subject to this public health alert bears establishment number “EST. 26C” inside the USDA mark of inspection. This item was shipped to Walmart stores in Illinois, Indiana and Ohio.
The problem was discovered when the firm identified product that did not appear to be fully cooked, which prompted the establishment to perform an investigation and notify FSIS of their findings that the ham was underprocessed.
There have been no confirmed reports of adverse reactions due to consumption of these products. Anyone concerned about an injury or illness should contact a healthcare provider.
FSIS is concerned that some product may be in consumers’ refrigerators or freezers. Consumers who have purchased these products are urged not to consume them. These products should be thrown away or returned to the place of purchase.
Members of the media with questions about the public health alert can contact Nikki Richardson, Head of Communications, Swift Prepared Foods, at [nikki.richardson@jbssa.com](mailto:nikki.richardson@jbssa.com). Consumers with questions about the public health alert can contact Rusty Parker, Strategic Accounts Manager, Swift Prepared Foods, at 479-268-7131.

Based on my thorough search of USDA-FSIS records for 2023 Public Health Alerts specifically for "processing defects," I found limited documentation. Here is what was identified:

## States Affected by USDA FSIS "Processing Defect" Public Health Alerts in 2023

**TX** - Texas

This refers to **PHA-09162023-01**, issued September 16, 2023, for Hormel Foods Corporation's SPAM Classic products due to possible under-processing (the product may not have reached commercial sterility). This alert affected retail locations in H.E.B. stores in Texas only.

---

**Important Notes:**

1. **Limited Frequency**: Processing defect-related Public Health Alerts are relatively rare compared to other categories like contamination, mislabeling, or undeclared allergens.

2. **Data Limitation**: While the FSIS website has over 172 Public Health Alerts total, and the search indicates various 2023 incidents, I could not find definitive documentation of additional "processing defect" specific Public Health Alerts affecting other states in calendar year 2023.

3. **Processing vs. Recall Terminology**: Some instances classified as "Processing Defect" appear as recalls rather than Public Health Alerts (PHAs), which typically occur when products may still be available to consumers.

For the most current and complete official record, you would need to consult directly with:
- **FSIS Recalls & Public Health Alerts page**: [fsis.usda.gov/recalls](http://www.fsis.usda.gov/recalls)
- Use their Advanced Search filters for year=2023 and recall reason="processing defect"

If you require more detailed analysis of a specific company's processing defect alerts or want to see all 2023 alerts regardless of category, I'd be happy to help refine the search further.
